name: Political Asylum (Law No. 11 of 2018)

qualifying_event.description: Qatar is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol and has no comprehensive refugee-status-determination law. Its only codified protection mechanism is Law No. 11 of 2018 on the Regulation of Political Asylum, which covers politically-motivated claims specifically, not the broader Refugee Convention persecution grounds (race, religion, nationality, social group).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Evidence of political persecution or well-founded fear thereof in the country of origin.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded claim of political persecution, assessed under Law No. 11 of 2018 -- narrower in scope than the 1951 Refugee Convention's persecution grounds.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of political persecution or well-founded fear

outcome.duration_length: not confirmed in this build -- open gap

STRUCTURAL FINDING: Qatar has NO general/comprehensive refugee-protection law -- Law No. 11/2018 covers only POLITICALLY-motivated claims, a narrower scope than the 1951 Convention's five persecution grounds, so this file should not be read as Qatar's equivalent of a full asylum system. Compare against Rwanda's genuine domestic system (rw_international_protection.json) or the UNHCR-mandate-in-absence-of-domestic-law pattern seen in Jordan/Mongolia/Cote d'Ivoire -- Qatar sits closer to the latter, with a codified but very narrow domestic law layered on top rather than a full determination system. Duration, renewability terms, and work/study/family rights on recognition were NOT disclosed by the available source -- all set to conservative defaults (none/restricted/false) pending verification, not sourced facts.
